messages:
anna: Heads-up — p95 latency on llm-llama3-13b climbed ~25% after yesterday's model-metadata push. Seen across dedicated and hosted. Started at ~11:40 PST.

mike: ugh. any perf traces? quick numbers?

anna: attaching brief profiler dump (GPU timeline + kernel selector log):
```
[profiler] seq_len=1024 batch=4 head_dim=128 hidden=5120
kernel_selector: candidate=fused_attn_v2 score=0.88 constraints=(supports_rmsnorm_silu=false)
kernel_selector: candidate=matmul_fallback score=0.92 constraints=(head_dim%32==0)
selected: matmul_fallback (reason: fused_attn_v2 reported constraints mismatch on rmsnorm_silu)
kernel_exec matmul_fallback dtype=float16 time=3.6ms tokens=512
fused_attn_v2 (not run) est_time=2.1ms
KV prefetch: windows=8 prefetch_bytes=48MB memcpy_count=12 thrash_warn=true

summary: selector picked slower kernel due to unexpected model flag (rmsnorm_silu=true) and our kernel table currently marks fused_attn_v2 as incompatible.
```

raj: that rmsnorm+SiLU combo was added for the new finetune checkpoint metadata, right? think we flipped `rmsnorm_silu` in the manifest yesterday.

julia: can we change selector logic to prefer fused_attn when it *would* be faster even if a minor flag mismatch exists? e.g. allow soft-constraints with heuristic penalty instead of hard exclude.

kevin: +1. also the KV prefetch looks noisy — memcpy_count=12 for a batch=4 steady-rate is suspicious. might be prefetch window misaligned with our cache lanes.

anna: note: these regressions show up at p95 for long chat sessions (seq>512). short seqs not affected. chat-template conversations with multi-round context are the main hit.

mike: suggestion: add a quick product of head_dim*seq_len threshold in the selector: if head_dim*seq_len > 131072 then force fused_attn candidate scoring boost (if the kernel supports it w/o extreme memory). avoids misclassifying typical Llama3-13b chat flows.

raj: agree. Also we should validate model metadata mapping — a lot of our kernel capability table uses `norm_type=rms` and an `activation=silu` flag but the manifest used `rmsnorm_silu=true` flattened. small naming mismatch triggers constraint failure. I'll add a compatibility mapper.

julia: actionable runtime config to try right now (hotfix):
```json
{"kernel_selector": {"soft_constraints": true, "soft_penalty": 0.15, "head_seq_boost_threshold": 131072}, "kv_cache": {"prefetch_windows": 4, "prefetch_bytes_cap": 24}}
```

kevin: also run a micro-warmup probe on new model versions: send 8 warmup requests at small seq (64) to exercise fused kernel path so JIT kernels get warmed and selector gets real latency samples. avoids cold-start fallback.

mike: good call. we should also include an integration test that uses head_dim variants (64/128/256) + seq 256/1024 to ensure selector picks the expected kernel. save as perf-ci test.

anna: I rolled a temporary revert on the model-manifest to previous metadata (runtime-bot handled it). p95 improved back to baseline.

runtime-bot: deploy:manifest-revert by anna at 2301003360. rollback-id=f3b2c4.

anna: next steps: (1) raj will add manifest->kernel capability mapper; (2) julia will land soft-constraints patch behind a flag; (3) kevin will add warmup probe + perf-ci tests; (4) ops reduce kv_prefetch windows as a short-term mitigation. I'll monitor p95 for the next 48h.

mike: can someone file a small perf-ticket with the profiler snippet and labels (llama3-13b, rmsnorm_silu, kv-prefetch)? I'll link it to the rollback.

raj: filing now. ticket: PERF-1257. adding kernel table diff and suggested mapper.

julia: landing draft PR for soft-constraints @ 2301003380, will mark as experimental.

kevin: I'll add warmup probe to canary pipeline tonight.

anna: thanks team. if anything spikes again, ping me and include the kernel_selector log. :thumbsup:
